reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data reported to confirm CD40 engagement by sotigalimab. Cannot assess whether the drug reached and modulated its intended target. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers or pharmacodynamic markers reported to assess whether CD40 agonism led to downstream immune activation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (ORR) clearly failed across all three cohorts with very low response rates: Cohort 1: 9.09%, Cohort 2: 7.69%, Cohort 3: 0%. PFS also failed across all cohorts with short durations (1.87-3.48 months). No clinical benefit demonstrated. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. All cohorts showed similarly poor outcomes. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm trial with no control group makes assessment challenging, but the ORR rates are well below historical benchmarks for melanoma (typically 15-25% for active agents). Trial was terminated for business reasons, not safety, suggesting the futility was clear. The serious adverse event rate appears high but without a control arm comparison, dose-limiting toxicity cannot be definitively established.

failure_modes.evidence: No biomarker data to assess target engagement or pathway modulation. Single-arm design with no control group limits interpretation of both efficacy and safety signals.
